newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bombardier in US$1.4 bln AMR jet deal.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier in US$1.4 bln AMR jet deal.

text.p: Bombardier Inc's Bombardier Regional Aerospace division said on Tuesday that AMR Corp's American Eagle regional airline affiliate had said it planned to buy 25 Canadian Regional Jet 70-seat airliners, with options on another 25, worth a total of US$1.4 billion.
Deliveries of the CRJ Series 700 to American Eagle are scheduled to commence in early 2001, Bombardier said.

"The Canadair Regional Jet Series 700 promises superior operating economies and efficiencies coupled with great passenger appeal. We are confident that the CRJ Series 700 will help strengthen our network as we enter the 21st century," said Peter Pappas, American Eagle's senior vice-president of planning.
Earlier on Tuesday American Eagle said it placed a US$1 billion order for short-range passenger jets with Brazil's state-owned Embraer SA.

"We are...gratified by the confidence that one of the world's premier regional airlines, known for its rigid technical criteria, has shown in our aircraft," said Pierre Lortie, president of Bombardier Regional Aircraft.

The Canadair Regional Jet Series 700 program was officially launched in January 1997 and has gathered 117 orders, options and memoranda of understanding from eight airlines on five continents. Certification to the latest FAA and JAA standards and initial deliveries are scheduled for the third quarter of the year 2000, Bombardier said.
The 70-seat jet is an extended version of Bombardier's 50-seat Canadian Regional Jet.
